findings.title: Stomp on soil with Unbreakable footing on: a harder stomp shakes the ground 5 times less, then stays flat at any effort, so the effort search and the page contradict themselves
findings.location: src/engine.js MOVES.stomp.blow (~lines 3786-3794, the round 4 cap: qultFor(surface, footB) x footArea x footPulse, applied once r.realBreaks); test/powers.js 5c 'same shaking' check (only asserts <= where real ground breaks)
findings.evidence: Engine (scratch e4.js/e6.js/e8.js, 10 ft Rex, comic mode, loose sand, unbreakable on). ppv at 5 m: 12.2 mm/s at log10 kg 2.96, then 2.48 mm/s from 2.98 up to 10^10 kg. With the power off it keeps rising: 12.3 at 3.0, 49.6 at 6, 3,920 at 10. Soft clay: 4.47 mm/s at every effort from 100 kg to 10^10 kg; off, 5.6 to 3,570 mm/s. Gravel and stiff clay also go flat. The page (Stomp, sand, 1,000 t dial) says opposite things at two nearby efforts. Custom 912 kg: 'The ground resists the foot with its strength plus its inertia ..., so the foot stops after about 8.8 cm' (the whole 6,380 kg·m/s goes in). Custom 1 t: 'Of that push (6,400 kg·m/s), the ground takes only what it can bear, 1,300 kg·m/s'. Plaster preset at 5 m: 'Even all-out, this move doesn't shake the ground enough that plaster may crack 5 m away'; with the power off it finds 58.2 t. Nearest people 1.5 m, all-out: 'Courtesy ceiling: 0.015% (lifting 149 kg). Past that, the ground shakes hard enough that plaster may crack 1.5 m away. Above the courtesy ceiling'. Yet all-out gives 6.7 mm/s and 'At this effort it also' doesn't list plaster. In the engine, plasterOver at 1.5 m is true up to log 2.97 and false from 2.99 to 6.
findings.expected: Brief 5c: the push still goes in, the ground 'shakes exactly as real physics says', and 'the effort and the not-so-heroic presets choose how hard'. A stronger stomp should never shake the ground less. Under canon's weak-ground exception the ground's take may stop growing, but it can't drop. Just below the print threshold the page itself says real sand stopped the whole 6,380 kg·m/s blow within 8.8 cm. One step harder, the cap counts static bearing only, about 20 kN against the roughly 99 kN the sand had just taken through its inertia. That gives a 5x drop and a ceiling that all-out never reaches. (presence.js checks that 'ground shaking never falls with more effort' only with the powers off.)
findings.fix: Make the cap continuous at the print: J_ground = min(J, max(qult·A·T, J_print)). J_print is the blow real ground stops within the kept print, from the page's own penetration law m v dv/dx = -A(q + ρv²): v_print² = (q/ρ)(exp(2ρA·print/m) - 1), J_print = m_eff·v_print. On clay (print 0) this is the static cap. Add a powers-on check to test/powers.js that each move's ppv at the nearest people never falls as effort rises, on sand, clay and concrete.

verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced in the engine and on the page. MOVES.stomp.blow switches to the static cap qult x footArea x footPulse once r.realBreaks is true. On sand that switch happens at the kept print (realHole > printCap = 90 mm). Just below it, real sand takes the whole blow, J = 6,388 kg·m/s over 64 ms (about 100 kN, 5 times its static bearing, through its inertia term). One step harder the cap allows only 1,297 kg·m/s. So ppv at 5 m falls from 12.2 to 2.48 mm/s and stays there up to 10^10 kg. Gravel has a smaller cliff (1.78 to 1.67 mm/s at 10^4.47 kg). Every other surface is monotonic.

Canon's weak-ground exception lets the ground's take stop growing. It cannot let a harder push give the ground less than real ground was just shown to bear. The page contradicts itself as a result (sand, nearest people 1.5 m, 1,000 t dial):
- All-out reads 'Courtesy ceiling: 0.015% (lifting 149 kg). Past that, the ground shakes hard enough that plaster may crack 1.5 m away. Above the courtesy ceiling'.
- Its 'At this effort it also ...' line lists only rattling, not plaster.
- Custom 912 kg lists plaster cracking at 1.5 m. Custom 1 t does not, and says 'the ground takes only what it can bear, 1,300 kg·m/s'.

powers.js 5c only asserts power-on <= power-off where real ground breaks, so it cannot catch a drop. No test checks the stomp's shaking against effort with the power on.

One part of the evidence is not a defect. The plaster preset at 5 m saying 'never' is still right after a fix: the continuous cap gives 12.2 mm/s at 5 m, below the 19.9 mm/s plaster limit at 1/64 ms. The defect is the drop and the ceiling contradiction.

findings.title: Jump landing on weak ground: Unbreakable footing lowers the shaking even where the real ground holds the landing
findings.location: src/engine.js MOVES.jump.shake (cap = o.unbreakable && r.landBear != null ? min(J, landBear·T) : J, applied to the feet's blow at every landing ratio); test/powers.js 5c 'same shaking' jump check (concrete only)
findings.evidence: Scratch e11.js, loose sand, comic. log10 kg 3.6: real landing ratio 0.929 (ground holds, sink 0). ppv at 5 m 1.42 mm/s with the power off, 1.34 with it on. At 3.65: ratio 0.977, 1.58 against 1.34. The feet's blow 2·legEff·v over footPulse is capped at landBear·footPulse = 10.9 kN x 64 ms, though the model says the ground bears this landing. README Known limits: 'it holds the ground only where real ground would break, by the ground hazard's own rule ... a dent ... is real and its energy goes into the ground as before.'
findings.expected: Where real ground doesn't give, the power changes nothing and the shaking matches the power-off value. That is brief 5c's test ('ppv at 5 m and the plaster reach match the shaking with it off for the same push') and the README's own rule.
findings.fix: Apply the landing cap only when r.landRatioReal > 1 (as the stomp gates on realBreaks), e.g. cap = (J, T) => (o.unbreakable && r.landRatioReal > 1 ? Math.min(J, r.landBear * T) : J). Extend the powers.js jump check to sand and soft clay.

verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced. MOVES.jump.shake applies cap(J, T) = min(J, landBear x T) to the feet's blow (2 legEff v over footPulse) at every landing ratio. The body pulse's cap binds only when landRatioReal > 1, which is algebraically the same condition. The feet pulse's cap binds earlier: on loose sand from landRatioReal of about 0.92, where the model says the ground bears the landing (sink 0).

For the same jump result, the capped landing gives:
- 1.342 mm/s at 5 m against 1.438 uncapped at landRatioReal 0.935.
- 1.342 against 1.647 at 0.999.
- At 1.5 m: 3.63 against 4.45 mm/s.

The displayed total with powers on (1.342) is below the powers-off total (1.417 to 1.579) at 10^3.6 to 10^3.65 kg. This breaks the README's rule that the power holds the ground 'only where real ground would break', and brief 5c's 'same shaking for the same push' where the ground bears it. The effect is small (sub-threshold mm/s on sand only), so minor.

The reviewer's proposed fix is wrong as written. Gating the cap on landRatioReal > 1 alone creates a 19% downward cliff at ratio 1: 1.647 to 1.342 mm/s between 10^3.650 and 10^3.655 kg, the same kind of defect as the stomp finding.

verdict.reasoning:

The brief's 5c test ('no move ... sinks into the ground') is satisfied by preventing sinking past the bearing; it does not require claiming zero depth.

On clay the stomp keeps no print (printCap 0), so 'no sinking' is consistent there. The defect is granular soil (sand, gravel) only. It is a wording and consistency error with no wrong numbers, so minor. The reviewer's engine change (keeping a print depth in jump, lift and throw) is more than needed.

findings.expected:
The ground can push sideways on a foot with at most Coulomb friction on the normal load it carries itself, mu × min(N, Nmax). The engine's own real-ground footing uses exactly that limit (anchorCapacity R2 = mu Nmax / cos θ). Canon (CLAUDE.md) says: 'Where the ground couldn't bear the push, their power supplies it.' That covers the sideways part as much as the downward part. Any grip beyond mu Nmax exists only because their power holds up the extra normal load, so it is their power's push, and it belongs in 'supplied'.
Capped at mu Nmax T, the sand's sideways take for the 100 t level throw is at most 23.4 kN × 0.155 s = 3,630 kg m/s (0.96 mm/s, no plaster), not 42,160. At 1e6 kg it is 1,505 kg m/s (2.9 mm/s, no plaster), not 140,100.

Change README and decision 22 to match. Add a powers.js check: on sand, no toGround's sideways part exceeds mu Nmax T.

verdict.reasoning:
Partly real. When Rex stands on friction alone (They take their own recoil off), the defect is real. When the power is on, which is the default, the behaviour is by design.

(a) Friction footing (own recoil off), with Unbreakable footing on. weakGround (engine.js 3475-3482) caps only the downward part at (bearing - weight) x T and hands the ground the sideways part whole. That sideways part is friction, and anchorCapacity (Nmax = Infinity under holdsGround) builds it on a normal load the engine itself says the ground does not carry: the downward excess is booked as 'supplied'. Friction from the ground can't exceed mu x the normal force the ground actually exerts, at most mu x Nmax.
- Car at 45 deg on loose sand at 1e6 kg: bear = max(0, 40.4 kN - (Rex + car) 42.6 kN) = 0, so the ground takes none of the downward push. Yet it is charged 82,211 kg m/s sideways over 64 ms, a mean 1.28 MN. The limit is mu x Nmax = 23.4 kN, so 1,505 kg m/s.

- The brief's 5c example list for 'couldn't bear the push' includes 'a sprint start', a sideways push. So canon's exception covers sideways grip beyond what the ground can give.

(b) Own recoil on, as if bolted. The finding's level throws, the 1e6 kg shove and the 1e9 kg Wrestle throw are all this default case, and here the whole sideways recoil going into the planet is what brief 5d says. 5d: 'Momentum is kept, not absorbed: the planet takes it, as with Bolted today ... a huge recoil is a huge jolt'; '5d keeps momentum (the planet takes it), so it is not an exception'. The shove with own recoil off is fine: N = W, and mu W (17.1 kN) < mu Nmax on sand. Severity is minor because only non-default footing is affected, though there the plaster reach is wrong by a large factor (37 m against none).

His legs spread the push into the ground over 64 ms, and over that time the ground can bear it, so it takes the whole push and shakes from it.' findings.expected: Decision 22 and the README call this 'one rule for every push': the ground takes at most its bearing beyond the weight on it × T of the downward part, plus the sideways part whole, and their power supplies the rest. That cap is finite: (1.55 MN − W) × 64 ms ≈ 97,000 kg·m/s on concrete. So a straight-up throw or toss at infinite strength should give the ground about what it gets at 10^30, not an unbounded push. The Throw text must not say the ground 'can bear' a push it calls ∞× its limit.
findings.fix: In weakGround, apply the cap to unbounded pushes too: when !isFinite(J) and T > 0, return { J: Jh (Infinity only if there is a sideways part, else 0) combined with cap, whole: Infinity, supplied: Infinity }, using `Jd = Infinity` whenever sin(th) > 0. The page then takes its suppliedText branch. Add a powers.js check that a vertical throw and a vertical toss at F = Infinity leave the ground ≤ bear × T.

verdict.reasoning: weakGround (engine.js 3476) starts with `if (!ctx.unbreakable || !isFinite(J) || ...) return { J }`, so an unbounded push skips the cap and the ground gets J = Infinity. Both the throw and the toss have a push time: T = max(limbPulse, push.t) = 64 ms. Decision 22 says the cap applies whenever there is a push time; only a push with none, as in the Jump's comic-infinite case, gives the ground nothing. The cap is finite: (1.55 MN - W) x 64 ms, about 97,000 kg·m/s on concrete. So at the Infinite dial a straight-up throw or toss should hand the ground about what it gets at 10^30 kg. Instead the page says plaster cracks 'out to the whole planet', where 10^30 gives 7.83 m and 7.68 m. The Throw item also contradicts itself: the push is '∞× what the concrete slab can carry' and in the next breath 'the ground can bear it'. For the partner toss this unbounded push is the tab's headline harm chip. The Jump tab at the same dial gives the ground none, so the rule is not applied the same way across tabs.
